A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LEANCODE work and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. The earlier appendix sections 8.1–8.5 correspond to Appendices A–E in v4.

before.justification: v1 reports original code-search and summarization experiments, GPT-4o transfer results, attention analyses, and the replacement study in Section 8.5.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results, including task performance, efficiency measurements, attention analyses, and the replacement study in Appendix E.

M1.justification: Category-local token weighting, task-specific attention sources, and token-level removal in Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. The added sentence describing the returned dataset only explains an existing algorithm step.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Java code search and summarization using the same CodeSearchNet-derived datasets and retain the GPT-4o transfer scenarios. No dataset, task, or evaluated population is added or removed.

E2.justification: DietCode, SlimCode, and the unsimplified Base condition remain in the corresponding comparisons in Tables 2–6. The DietCode removal-algorithm replacement comparison in Table 10 is also retained.

E3.justification: The dataset splits in Table 9, 10%–50% removal settings, model configurations, metrics, and GPT-4o testing procedures remain unchanged, including the 400-pair code-search evaluation.

E4.justification: The attention-distribution analyses, code examples, transferability evaluation, and replacement study test the same questions with the same evidence. Section 8.5 becomes Appendix E without changing its ablation.

E5.justification: Attention-score variance summaries and distribution plots are unchanged. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the task-performance comparisons.

E6.justification: Tables 1–10 retain their numerical entries and findings. For example, at 50% removal, LEANCODE's CodeBERT search MRR remains 0.688 and its CodeT5 summarization BLEU remains 18.46; transfer and replacement-study results also match.

T1.justification: The removal objective, global and category-local averages, and attention definitions in Equations 1–6 are unchanged in substance. No formal assumption, theorem, proof, or derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same methodological and transferability claims, including the stated improvements over DietCode and SlimCode. Wording and heading edits do not change their scope.

C2.justification: Explanations involving context-sensitive importance, truncation, SlimCode's priority levels, and GPT-4o behavior remain the same. Section 7 retains the Java-only, generalizability, and timing limitations.

D1.justification: The reported optimizer, learning rates, hardware, attention-collection timing, GPT-4o prompts, dataset statistics, and source references remain unchanged. No implementation or code/data access information is added or removed.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to DietCode, SlimCode, other simplification approaches, and pretrained code models remain unchanged in the introduction, related work, and appendices.

P1.justification: v4 makes limited sentence edits, expands the explanation of Algorithm 1, updates author/contact text, and renames Section 4.1. Appendix numbering changes from 8.1–8.5 to A–E, with corresponding cross-reference updates; the narrative order is retained.

P2.justification: v4 reformats the author block, enlarges Tables 7–8 and Figure 8, and moves Tables 9–10 into compact single-column placement alongside the final appendix text. Figure content and table data remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v4 provides light wording and navigation cleanup and larger attention-statistics displays, while making Tables 9–10 more compact. The scientific arguments, evidence, reproducibility information, and limitations remain unchanged. These modest presentation tradeoffs produce no meaningful net difference in overall quality.
